chapter: Rhythm Club memories and playing technique
title: Pete Brown and the riff altoists

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Oh Pete Brown, oh yeah, I made a lot of

records with Pete Brown. Pete Brown did a lot of records with Teddy Wilson, then he did a lot with I think it was, oh Frank Newton and of course Procope's an old hand at the game. But Pete Brown, I did so many dates with Pete.
Pete was a very jovial person, wasn't he?

Yes, he was, and he was five times bigger than that little alto saxophone he played. But he could swing, he could really play. He was a good riff man. He always used to--well in the record dates I was on, whoever was leading would tell Pete to set a riff for the rest of the band and he was a good riff man just to set a riff and everybody start riffing behind him.
Why do you think he never became better known?
I don't know. Because at the time, see, there were quite a few boys around there playing the same as Pete, riffing, a boy by the name of Charlie Holmes.
What's his name, Charlie Holmes, Tab Smith. See all those boys were all good riff men, too, and there was quite a few of them around there. Tab Smith made a great little name for himself.
Right. Then of course there was Hodges and Benny Carter...

Oh yeah, well, but that was another league altogether, Hodges and Benny Carter. But these are, the boys that I just mentioned was in sort of would you say the minor league, but they were good. Charlie Holmes, Tab Smith, oh George.... See a lot of these guys, there was a drummer around by the name of Dinah. I never did know Dinah's first name because everybody called him just Dinah. And another one around then named Puss Johnson, I never did know his name. Right today I don't know Puss Johnson's name, his real name. Like a lot of people don't know my real name because all they've heard is Cozy Cole. Somebody say well who is William Cole, they wouldn't know.
But at least they have a first name for you.
Oh yes. Oh that bass player's name is bugging me now, I can't think of it. Former Cab Calloway bass player. Can't think of it.
